title: Marcos: ASEAN, China to finalize 'definition of terms' as COC reaches 85%-90%
summary: ASEAN and China are now finalizing the "definition of terms" in the South China Sea Code of Conduct, as the negotiations failed to be completed under the Philippines' chairmanship.

blocks.text: Marcos said there are terms in the COC that need to accepted by the parties. JAM STA ROSA/ Pool via REUTERS

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China are now finalizing the "definition of terms" in the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC), as the negotiations failed to be completed under the Philippines' chairmanship.

During a press briefing following the culmination of the ASEAN Summit, Marcos said there are terms that need to be understood and norms accepted by the parties, noting that the negotiations has reached 85%-90% under the Philippines' ASEAN chairmanship.

The COC was earlier described as "80% complete," with Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro saying it is now expected to be finished during Singapore's chairmanship of ASEAN next year. The Philippines maintains that non-completion is not a failure, citing time constraints. — BM, GMA News
